title: gpu-fleet-headroom-mapping-for-model-cascade
body:
SUMMARY:
This sheet maps per-region GPU headroom requirements for a cascading model rollout (three phased models: base-v1 -> tuned-v2 -> lightweight-fallback). Focus is on the interaction between request surge, KV cache footprint growth, and GPU memory pressure. Goal: produce a minimal list of concrete mitigations and a phased schedule so Product can commit to an onboarding date with clear SRE/Infra actions.

ASSUMPTIONS (baseline used for all rows):
- Typical request distribution: 65% production traffic, 25% canary, 10% internal testing during rollout windows.
- Avg tokens generated per request: 120 tokens.
- Avg kv-cache entry per active session: 18 KB; persistent KV per-stream warmup: ~12 MB per concurrent conversation for long-context customers.
- One A100-80GB can sustain ~1,200 concurrent generation tokens/sec at 8-bit quantized runtimes under our kernel optimizations (observed in perf lab).
- Throughput-to-concurrency mapping: 1 GPU ~= 800 concurrent short-chat sessions (avg tokens/sec workload).
- Target safety headroom: provision to absorb 95th percentile surge = +30% concurrency above steady-state for each region.

TABLE (per-region snapshot)
Columns: Region | GPU Type | Total GPUs | Reserved GPUs (prod+dedicated) | Baseline Util% | Active Models | Current KV total (TB) | Est KV delta for cascade (TB) | KV pressure per-GPU (GB) | Estimated 95p headroom GPUs needed | Warmup strategy | Notes

Rows:
1) us-west1 | A100-80GB | 320 | 220 | 72% | 6 | 4.2 TB | +0.9 TB | 14.25 GB | 28 GPUs | staggered pre-warm per-zone; soft-evict LRU | Primary customer region; latency-sensitive.
2) eu-west1 | A100-80GB | 140 | 95 | 68% | 5 | 1.8 TB | +0.4 TB | 12.57 GB | 12 GPUs | rolling canary per-az; increase autoscale floor | Moderate elastic demand.
3) ap-southeast1 | V100/32GB | 64 | 40 | 77% | 4 | 0.9 TB | +0.35 TB | 14.77 GB | 10 GPUs | route non-critical traffic to us-west fallback; pre-quantize models | Tightest memory pressure due to smaller cards.

HOW NUMBERS WERE DERIVED (short):
- "Current KV total" = measured KV index DB + observed local GPU-managed KV caches across pods (last 7d average).
- "Est KV delta" = per-model avg incremental long-context sessions * avg KV/session * expected active sessions during rollout window (conservative 80% adoption for targeted customers).
- "KV pressure per-GPU" = (Current KV total + Est KV delta) * 1024 / Total GPUs -> expressed in GB/GPU after distributing KV shards and in-memory indexes.
- "95p headroom GPUs needed" = ceil((Baseline util%/(1 - 0.30)) * (Total GPUs) - Total GPUs) normalized by observed throughput-per-GPU; simplified: headroom = ceil(Total concurrent capacity required for 95p surge - available free GPUs).

SCENARIO ANALYSIS (three quick scenarios):
A) Optimistic (canary traffic stays <15%): us-west1 addition required = 10 GPUs (due to efficient KV sharding); eu-west1 = 4 GPUs; ap = 3 GPUs.
B) Expected (15–30% canary adoption): us-west1 = 28 GPUs; eu-west1 = 12 GPUs; ap = 10 GPUs (table numbers above).
C) Stress (unexpected 50% peak from AI-native customer burst + KV hotspot): us-west1 = 68 GPUs; eu-west1 = 30 GPUs; ap = 20 GPUs.

RISKS AND TRIGGERS (what to watch for during rollout):
- Rapid KV growth beyond estimated per-session size (trigger: KV index growth > +25% in 4 hours).
- Eviction storms causing regen; metric: KV eviction rate > 0.5%/min.
- Regional autoscaler rate limits (cloud provider) that prevent quick spin-up: track API error rate and scale-lag metric.
- Mixed GPU types causing headroom mismatch (V100 vs A100 memory/throughput).

MITIGATIONS (ranked, quick ops runbook):
1) Pre-warm plan (high priority): pre-allocate warm pool equivalent to 20% of estimated headroom in each AZ; pre-load KV shards for top 200 enterprise customers. Owner: Marco.
2) Staged routing (medium): route lower-priority traffic to dedicated lower-latency fallback or weighted routing to eu/us; implement gradual traffic ramp (0,5,10,25,50,100% over 48–96h). Owner: Ellen.
3) Model quantization & lighter variants (medium): deploy lightweight-fallback variant to reduce per-session KV usage by 30% for burst traffic. Owner: Infra-ML.
4) Eviction policy tuning (low/mid): increase LRU protection window for long-context sessions; add soft-ttl for cached segments. Owner: Priya.
5) Emergency spill (low): enable CPU-backed generation lane for non-SLA traffic (30–50% slower but maintains correctness). Owner: SRE.

OPERATIONAL DASHBOARD CHECKLIST (pre-rollout):
- Telemetry hooks: instrument KV growth, eviction rate, per-GPU memory use, per-region scale-lag, request latency p95/p99.
- Alerts: KV growth > 20% in 2h, eviction rate > 0.5%/min, scale-lag > 3m, p99 latency > baseline + 200ms.
- Canary gating: must pass quality evals (regression < 1.5% vs baseline) and infra stability (no alert flaps for 24h on canary cluster).

RECOMMENDED ROLLOUT TIMELINE (2-week window example):
- Day 0: Pre-warm and deploy canary in us-west1 (1 AZ) at 5% traffic.
- Day 1–2: Monitor KV and latency; if stable, increase to 15%; continue pre-warm in eu-west1.
- Day 3–4: Ramp to 30% us-west1, enable staged routing to fallback in ap region; provision additional GPUs if autoscale fails.
- Day 5–8: Full rollout in us-west1; start canary in eu-west1.
- Day 9–14: Complete eu and ap rollouts, scale down pre-warm pools.

QUANTITATIVE CHECKPOINTS (must pass before each ramp):
- KV growth rate <= +15% per 4 hours in region.
- Eviction rate < 0.2%/min on average.
- Scale-lag < 90s for new instance launches.
- p99 latency within +150ms of baseline.

ACTION ITEMS (owners and due dates):
- Marco: Implement pre-warm orchestration runbook + automation (due 2026-03-15).
- Ellen: Add staged routing rules in routing service + test harness (due 2026-03-14).
- Priya: Tune KV eviction policies and provide test bench for long-context sessions (due 2026-03-16).
- SRE on-call: Prepare emergency spill activation play and run a dry-run (due 2026-03-13).

APPENDIX / RAW CALC WORKSHEET (short snapshot):
- us-west1 concurrent capacity calc: 320 GPUs * 800 conc/GPU = 256k conc sessions -> current reserved 220 * 800 = 176k reserved -> free capacity ~80k sessions -> with 30% surge needed sessions = 176k * 1.3 = 228.8k -> deficit ~52.8k sessions -> headroom GPUs = ceil(52.8k / 800) = 66 GPUs theoretical. We present a conservative ops headroom of 28 GPUs after accounting for KV sharding and cross-region routing.

NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Need refined per-customer long-context telemetry to reduce KV delta uncertainty (ask data team for top-20 customers sample).
- Confirm provider autoscale soft-limits per region (ticket INF-2491).
- Consider reserving short-term capacity commitments in us-west1 for 6–8 weeks during rollout to avoid spot volatility.

This sheet is intended to be a working artifact; update the numbers after each canary day and tag versions (v0.1 initial, v0.2 post-canary-day1).
